x: Darryl Maynard had a fine debut in the 'A' 800m. Ossie Cham made an impressive entrance with a brilliant 2.10m for 2nd place in the High Jump being ably backed up by Leroy Haughton.

Our middle distance men rallied well with Darryl Maynard standing in at 20 minutes notice to gain good 800 m points while we won both 1500m's with Stuart Paton gaining a faster win in the 'B' than Andy LLoyd in 'A' - but Andy then ran the 'A' 5000 some 30 minutes later to record a very creditable 14.04.

Following victory in the men's event in 1984 Belgrave has always been there or thereabouts but finished 6th in 1990 due in part to Darryl Maynard having the baton knocked out of his hand on the first 800m leg and trailing home in 42nd place.
The take-over zone. In the middle of the melee Jay Busk hands the baton to Darryl Maynard in BAL match 1.

If new member Steve Harris, who placed 5th, had been eligible for the race (we believe he will be for the next) we would have won the match. Track star Darryl Maynard came all the way down from Leeds to compete - and didn't score!
Duane Hart, Darryl Maynard, Rob Turner and Jon Ridgeon just had to run at their very best for us to win and this they did with an exceptionally fine 3:14.4.
Darryl Maynard at last ran an 800m as we know he can and although wishing he'd run the 'A' race was the first to admit we gained 4 points by running Dave Scott in the 'A'.
